title: suderra.edge-update.v1 device-bound agent update request
description: Signed by the edge-provisioning key, pinned in the OS image (ADR-048 DEC-2.4, DEC-2.9, DEC-3.3, DEC-22). It authorizes one device to replace its agent release: it binds a device (device_binding, device_id, tenant_id) to one release statement by statement digest and to the artifact's download location, under a monotonic update_seq. The agent only carries it to the update channel (channels.json update_channel); root verifies it itself and installs through the one installer. The acceptance window is the maintenance window: root accepts the statement only while not_before <= now < expires_at, so an update never applies outside the window the cloud chose (DEC-13.4). Unlike the provisioning manifest it carries no nonce, no site config and no trust-anchors bundle: it changes the agent binary and nothing else, and it carries no token or credential. The release statement is fetched by root from release_statement.url and must have the named digest. This v1 has no approvals member: the two-person approval is enforced server-side in P1; the planned suderra.edge-update.v2 carries a required approvals[] that root verifies against update-approver anchors, and a payload-version ratchet then refuses v1 (statements.json planned_successors).

update_seq.description: Monotonic per device and payload kind: root keeps the last accepted value in /data/suderra/os/seq/edge-update and accepts only a larger one (DEC-2.4).

release_statement.description: The suderra.edge-release.v1 statement this update installs: its statement digest, and where root fetches the envelope (the statement beside the artifact, artifact-naming.json statement). Root refuses a statement whose digest differs (release-digest-mismatch), so the location carries no trust.

artifact_url.description: Download location of the release artifact; integrity comes from the release statement, never from this URL (as in the provisioning manifest).

local_approval.description: True when root applies the update only after a local operator approval (DEC-13.4); false when the maintenance window alone authorizes it. An active alarm or a forced value blocks the update in both cases (maintenance-blocked).

max_outage_seconds.description: Outage budget: the longest the agent may be down for this update (agent restart, shutdown safe-state to the first control tick). Root and the health window enforce it (DEC-2.7, DEC-13.4).
